A 256-byte lookup indexed by screen character value. The resident code at $6F59–$6F5F reads a character from the selected screen buffer and writes the corresponding table byte to colour RAM. The table continues across $8000.
Continuation of the character-to-colour lookup beginning at $7FCF; this byte is entry $31 of that table, and entries continue through $80CE.

A 256-byte attribute table indexed by the map's metatile value. The downward movement check at $0C57 tests bits 0–1, and the horizontal movement checks at $0EB8 and $1051 test bit 1 when clipping the player against a tile.
A 256-byte table of top-left character codes indexed by a metatile value. The resident draw loop at $6D4D writes the selected code to the first cell of a two-by-two screen block.
A 256-byte table of top-right character codes indexed by a metatile value. The resident draw loop at $6D53 writes the selected code to the cell to the right of the first cell.
A 256-byte table of bottom-left character codes indexed by a metatile value. The resident draw loop at $6D5A writes the selected code one 40-character screen row below the first cell.
A 256-byte table of bottom-right character codes indexed by a metatile value. The resident draw loop at $6D60 writes the selected code one row below and one cell to the right of the first cell.

Load 12 update entry: load X from $4DBD and write $05 to $4DCB,X. It jumps to $0732 when row $6F3D equals $09 and column $6F3C is at least $09 and below $0C; otherwise it jumps to $0200. The entry bytes also belong to the captured character-copy source. The entry was reached during the bounded 200-frame capture and monitor collection. The conditions are tested with controlled inputs; this does not establish a natural route to them.

Load 12: the type-$01 vector in $7EDF/$7F0F selects this dispatcher. It reads $1AB1,X into Y, patches the jump at $A262 from the split tables at $A265/$A268, and jumps to the selected handler. The state index is not locally bounded; only three captured table pairs are described.
Absolute jump patched through operands $A263/$A264; the entry snapshot placeholder is $FF00.
Three captured low bytes of state targets, paired with high bytes at $A268: $A26B, $A2D0, $A307. State index bounds and ordinary-play reachability remain open.
Three captured high bytes paired with low bytes at $A265: $A26B, $A2D0, $A307. State index bounds and ordinary-play reachability remain open.

State 0: if $1A29,X is zero, go directly to the flag setter at $A2C5. Otherwise call $792C and $732A. If $732A returns carry set, a positive $1A6D,X selects state 1; zero or negative stores 8 at $1B17,X and selects state 2. If carry is clear, call $7227; when that returns carry set, call $5D7A with A=4. Continue at $A298. External callbacks and ordinary-play reachability remain open.

If $1AD3,X is zero, toggle bit 1 of $1AE4,X and set $1AD3,X to 3. Decrement $1AD3,X. Call $72FC: carry set selects 0 and clear selects 8 for $1B28,X. Clear carry, add $19E5,X and $1AE4,X to that value in sequence, propagating carry, and store the low byte at $19C3,X. This binary arithmetic assumes decimal mode is clear.
Set $1A7E,X to 1 only when it is zero, then return.
State 1: if $1A8F,X is zero, store state 0 and return. Otherwise pass A=8 to $45BC if $1B28,X is nonzero or $4574 if it is zero, then continue at $A2ED.

Set $1AD3,X to 2; exclusive-OR $1AC2,X with 2 and store it. Clear carry and add 4, $1B28,X and $19E5,X in sequence, carrying between additions, then store the low byte at $19C3,X and return. This binary arithmetic assumes decimal mode is clear.
State 2 decrements $1B17,X with eight-bit wrap. If nonzero, branch to the frame update at $A2ED. If zero, call $4B0E with A=$20 and jump to $5DB9 with A=1. Ordinary-play reachability remains open.
